key_insight: Capability emergence in language models follows a no-partial-credit, driven-nucleation process: all critical circuit parts must align before the capability appears.
engineering_relevance: This provides a rate-law framework for predicting when capabilities will emerge or be lost, enabling more controlled training, monitoring, and circuit-level intervention.
method: Analyzed circuit alignment and ablation behavior across multiple capabilities and model scales.
Fit a preregistered rate equation with frozen constants to forward, backward, and completion-based training scenarios.
Validated the mechanism in a controlled gated-attention model and tested targeted re-initialization of circuit slices.
evidence_signal: Across seven capabilities and three scales, single-part ablations left a median 17% of the capability instead of the 50–83% expected under partial-credit models, and the proposed law predicted emergence timing with about 5% median error on six held-out models.
watch_item: The framework is strongest for conjunction-style circuits and controlled settings, so generalization to broader model behaviors and interventions may be limited.
paper_title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
